lesson.title: Pointers, frames and a buffer overflow
lesson.goal: See that a pointer holds the place of a byte, that a stack frame lays its variables side by side, and that writing past a buffer overwrites its neighbour.

say: main has one local variable, a pointer called p. It asks malloc for six bytes on the heap, and p now points at the first one.
Writing through p fills the block with hello. Add four to p, and it points at the letter o.
main calls greet. Its frame holds a four byte buffer and, right after it, the return address back to main.
greet copies six letters into the four byte buffer. The last two run past its end and overwrite the return address.
Now free gives the heap block back. p still points into it, so p is a dangling pointer.
